faqs.a: Because email clients are stuck in 1999. Gmail strips <style> blocks, Outlook uses Word's rendering engine, and every client handles CSS differently. Tables plus inline styles are the only combination that works everywhere, which is exactly what this tool generates.
faqs.q: Why does the code use tables instead of modern CSS?

faqs.a: Deliberately not. Most email clients block images by default, so a logo shows as a broken box to many recipients. Text-only signatures always render and never trigger spam filters. Add your website link instead; interested people will click through.
